Rohilla Uid No: 02401R1091782006 In The Matter Of Smt. Seema Sharma W/O Sh Krishan Kumar Sharma D/O Sh Bhupal Sharma R/O B972, Shashtri Nagar, Delhi 52 ...... Compla Versus 1. Sh Krishan Kumar Sharma S/O Sh Bhudev Prasad 2. Sh Bhudev Prasad S/O Sh Shanti Ram 3. Sh Pawan Kumar Sharma S/O Sh Bhudev Prasad All R/O C178/11, Gali No. 7, (Opposite Ps Bhajan Pura), Bhajanpura, Delhi At Present R/O C255, Gali No. 2, Bhajanpura, Delhi. .....Respon Date Of Institution : 28.11.2006 Date On Which Matter Was Reserved For Order
texts.facts: Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52538181/ 1 1. The present complaint has been filed by the complainant under section 12 of Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against the respondents, respondent no.1 is the husband and other respondents are the in laws of the complainant. The brief facts of the case as have been disclosed in the complaint, wherein, it is stated that the marriage between the complainant and the respondent no.1 was solemnized on 12.12.2002 at Shashtri Nagar, Delhi according to Hindu rites and ceremonies. Two children Master Mayank and Master Kartikeya were born out of this wedlock, who are now in the care and custody of the complainant. It is stated that the father of the complainant had spent a huge amount and solemnized the marriage with great pomp and show. The parents of the complainant gave numerous dowry articles to respondent no. 1 and his family members including furniture, jewelery articles of gold and silver etc in the marriage. 2. It is further stated that after the marriage, for some weeks everything went on well but after a few weeks, the respondent no. 2 & 3, who were in domestic relationship with the complainant, started harassing and torturing the complainant with one way or the other and continued to inflict the acts of domestic violence upon the complainant. When the complainant was pregnant with first child , then the respondent no. 1 got her fallen from his moving motor bike intentionally and thus endangered the safety and life of the complainant and caused the domestic violence to her. Thereafter the acts of the domestic violence were continuously inflicted upon the complainant by the respondent no.1, his mother, sister along with the respondent no. 2 & 3. It is further stated that respondent no. 1 to 3 along with the mother and sister of the respondent no. 1 were not satisfied with the dowry articles which were given to them at the time of marriage with complainant. The respondent no. 1 CC No. 49/1/08 PS: Sarai Rohilla Seema Sharma Vs. Krishan Kumar Sharma & Ors. used to beat the complainant on one pretext or the other. It is further stated that the respondent no. 1 along with respondent no. 2 & 3 expressed their intention to purchase a plot in the Bhajanpura area and demanded a sum of Rs. 50,000/ from the complainant and asked her to demand the money from her parents in a very rude and compelling manner and a great mental harm was caused to her and consequently she demanded the money from her parents and she handed over Rs. 30,000/ to them. During the cause of the continuing harassment and abuse verbal as well as mental meted out to the complainant, in the month of November, 2005, the respondent no. 1 forced her to demand Rs. 2,00,000/ from her parents and due to the constraints and verbal abuse by the respondent no. 1 to 3 along with her mother in law, she handed over Rs. 1,40,000/ to the respondents, who demanded the amount on the pretext of construction of a house. It is further stated that at the birth of the first child of the complainant from the respondent no. 1, the complainant was subjected to harassment and slapped by her mother in law saying that whatever her parents wanted to give in " Pillia" ceremony, must provide in cash to her. Then in spite of numerous request by the complainant, no efforts were made by the respondent no. 1 to rescue her from the ongoing physical and verbal abuse by his mother and sister. 3. It is further stated that the respondent no. 2 quarreled with the parents of the complainant at the time of " Pillia" ceremony and demanded cash instead of customary items. After the the ceremony, the complainant was verbally abused and nothing was provided to her in the dinner and on the next day she was made to call her parents by the respondent no. 1 & 2 and sent from the matrimonial The Present Complaint Has Been Filed By ... vs Krishan Kumar Sharma & Ors on 28 August, 2014 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52538181/ 2 house along with her brother intentionally and no body came from the respondent's side to take her back into the matrimonial home. The respondent no. 1 ignored his matrimonial obligations and turned a deaf ear from the complainant. The respondent no. 1 to 3 along with the other CC No. 49/1/08 PS: Sarai Rohilla Seema Sharma Vs. Krishan Kumar Sharma & Ors. members of the shared household continued this sort of harassment in numerous ways. 4. It is further stated that in the month of December 2005, the complainant was mercilessly beaten by her mother in law, sister in law & the respondent no. 2 abused her verbally and made her to call her parents. At this when the parents and brother of the complainant reached for knowing the well being of her, they were also subjected to beatings by the respondent and medicolegal examinations were conducted. On 21.12.2005, police personnel of PS Bhajanpura got a compromise effected between the parties, but in defiance of the compromise , no body from the respondent side including the respondent no. 1 came to bring her back to matrimonial house/shared household rather the complainant when visited herself along with her brother to the matrimonial house, she was beaten mercilessly by the respondent no. 1 & 2 along with her mother in law and sister in law. When she demanded her " istridhan" they denied and claimed her entire istridhan as theirs and turned out the complainant from the shared household/matrimonial house along with two minor children in one single Saree and threatened her for life and to trap the parental family of the complainant in some false case. 5. It is further stated that the respondents are the proprietors of the two houses (i) C178/11, Gali no. 7, Bhajanpura, Delhi (ii) 227/30A, Gamri Road, Som Bazar Wali Gali, Bhajanpura, Delhi but the respondents are now living in rented accommodation at C255, Gali No. 12, Bhajanpura, Delhi in the shared household. The respondent no. 1 is running two coaching centers and earning a handsome amount of about Rs. 30,000/ per month. While the complainant is presently residing at her parental house and is a burden upon her parents and has no shelter and is deprived of her economic status along with her two minor children due to the acts and omission of domestic violence of the respondents. It is further stated that a FIR No. 220/06, u/s 498A/406/34 IPC CC No. 49/1/08 PS: Sarai Rohilla Seema Sharma Vs. Krishan Kumar Sharma & Ors. has been lodged against the respondents and a case u/s 125 Cr.P.C has been filed by the complainant against the respondent no. 1 which is pending adjudication and so far no maintenance is granted to her as the case is pending u/s 9 of the HMA Act, 1955, which has been filed by the respondent no. 1 with malafide intention against the complainant to escape the liabilities of the other case. 6. The following orders have been requested to be passed : The Present Complaint Has Been Filed By ... vs Krishan Kumar Sharma & Ors on 28 August, 2014 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52538181/ 3 (a) Protection order under section 18 of the act thereby prohibiting the respondents from committing any acts of domestic violence, alienating the properties and istridhan articles without the leave of the court, from committing the acts of domestic violence upon the complainant, her relatives and two minor children, (b) Residence order under section 19 of the act thereby directing the respondents to provide sufficient and reasonable accommodation to the complainant and children from any of the two houses, restraining the respondents from dispossessing the complainant alongwith her two children from the shared household, restraining the respondents from alienating or disposing of the shared household or encumbering the same, restraining them from renouncing their rights in the shared household except with the leave of the court, (c) Monetary relief under section 20 of the act, thereby directing the respondents to meet the expenses incurred and losses for the upbringing of minor children, (d) Compensation order under section 22 of the act for causing mental torture and emotional distress caused by the acts of domestic violence by the complainant. 7. Notice to the complaint was directed to be served upon the respondents by my Ld. Predecessor, who were served, appeared before the court and CC No. 49/1/08 PS: Sarai Rohilla Seema Sharma Vs. Krishan Kumar Sharma & Ors. expressed their willingness to contest the petition. Reply has been filed by the respondents wherein they have stated that the Domestic violence Act, 2005 is only prospective in operation and not retrospective in operation. The respondents have further claimed that the complainant is not entitled to any relief as she herself left the matrimonial home without any sufficient reason by executing document dated 21.12.2005, which bears the signatures of the parents and brothers of the complainant, wherein she has acknowledged that she was going to her parental house with her own free will and shall come back after few days but subsequently, she refused to join back the company of the respondent no.1. 8. The respondent no.1 has denied running two coaching center and earning Rs 30,000/per month and claimed only giving tuitions by visiting at the houses of the intending houses of lower classes occasionally as and when the same is demanded. It is further claimed that H. No. C178/10, Gali No. 7 & H. No. C178/11, Gali No.7, Bhajanpura, Delhi belong to his parents and he has been debarred and disowned by them. The Present Complaint Has Been Filed By ... vs Krishan Kumar Sharma & Ors on 28 August, 2014 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52538181/ 4 9. Since maintenance order was already passed in connected petition CC No. 49/1/08 PS: Sarai Rohilla Seema Sharma Vs. Krishan Kumar Sharma & Ors. filed u/s 125 Cr. PC hence the present case was fixed for complainant evidence. 10. The complainant was granted several opportunities for leading evidence in support of her case but she did not avail those opportunities. Thereafter, vide order dated 24.08.2011, the right to lead complainant evidence was closed however, at the request of the complainant, Ld. Predecessor permitted that the complainant evidence led in connected case under section 125 Cr. PC be read in the present case also. In the said petition, the complainant has examined herself as PW1 and tendered her evidence by way of affidavit Ex PW1/A, bearing her signatures at point A & B. PW1/complainant was subjected to cross examination by the respondents. The respondents did not lead evidence in support of their case despite availing number of opportunities, therefore, vide order dated 04.05.2012, respondent evidence was closed. subsequent thereto, matter was fixed for final arguments, which were tendered on behalf of both the parties except respondent no. 1. 11.
texts.arguments: It is further claimed that the respondent no.1 is residing at the rented accommodation @ Rs 1000/ pm and preparing for M.A examination and expenses for the same are required but he is financially very tight. The respondent no.1 is mentally disturbed and therefore unable to do tuition job properly and hardly earning Rs 2000/ to Rs 3000/ per month. It is claimed that the complainant is gainfully employed and earning Rs 10,000/pm and father of the complainant is in the business of dairies and the complainant is one of the partners in the said business. It is also claimed that the complainant is doing tuition job and getting Rs 6,000/ to 7,000/ per month. The petitioner has preferred replication wherein the assertions to the contrary have been controverted and has reiterated the facts stated in the petition. During the course of arguments, Ld. Counsel for the complainant submitted that the complainant has been able to prove her case against the respondents and she is entitled to receive all the orders as mentioned in the petition. It was further submitted that during the course of trial, the respondent no.1 offered to settle the matter and at his request some time was given to him but later on, he retracted and flatly refused to settle the matter. It was further submitted that in Execution petition bearing no.14/08 of HMA petition, the court had observed that public notice regarding disowning and debarring of respondent no.1 was only eyewash in order to defy the coercive process issued by the court. It was also submitted that no evidence in support of counter claim has been filed by the respondents and therefore, the case of complainant stands proved. 12. On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for respondent no.2 and 3 submitted CC No. 49/1/08 PS: Sarai Rohilla Seema Sharma Vs. Krishan Kumar Sharma & Ors. that there is not even a single specific allegations of harassment or violence having been committed upon the complainant by them. The evidence adduced in the connected petition cannot be relied upon as the said case was filed against respondent no. 1. It was further submitted that the sole allegation against respondent no.2 and 3 which find mention in the present complaint is at para no.11 that the complainant had filed a case FIR No.220/06, PS: Sarai Rohilla under section 498 /406/34 IPC for demand of dowry and harassment for not fulfilling the same however , both the respondents have already been discharged in the said case vide order dated 15.12.09 and said discharge order was upheld even by Hon'ble Sessions Court vide its order dated 19.05.2010 and thus, the present complaint is not maintainable against the respondent no.2 and 3. It was also submitted that the complainant's claim to reside at aforementioned properties is not maintainable as her Civil Suit seeking permanent and mandatory injunction has also been dismissed. Moreover, the complainant has not filed and proved any document to show that said properties belong to her husband and he has right thereof being coparcener. During cross examination, she has admitted The Present Complaint Has Been Filed By ... vs Krishan Kumar Sharma & Ors on 28 August, 2014 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52538181/ 5 this fact also. Ld. Counsel for respondent no.2 and 3 have placed reliance upon the judgment of RENU MITTAL Vs ANIL MITTAL & ORS , DOD:27.09.2010 & SR BATRA Vs TARUNA BATRA, DOD: 15.12.2006 13. The complainant/PW1 has further deposed that after she became pregnant, the respondents and other in laws did not take pity upon her and she was forced and compelled to do the entire household work and she was not given proper food and diet and medical aid as required. She has further deposed that it was the regular practice of the respondent and other in laws to beat her in furtherance of dowry demands and she was regularly sent to her parental house to fulfill the said demand. 16. She has further deposed that after the birth of second child, attitude and conduct of the respondent became more indifferent and due to non fulfillment of demand, the respondent used to remain annoyed with her and her sons. She has further deposed that on 23.09.2005, a compromise took place between them before SHO PS Bhajanpura and she was taken back to matrimonial house but on the very same day, she was beaten by the respondent, his brother and sister and was forced to bring money from her parental house. When she refused, she was threatened to be divorced. She has further deposed that on 21.12.2005, she was beaten by her mother in law and sister in law. On intimation when her brother, mother, father and one neighbour reached at matrimonial house, they were also humiliated, insulted and beaten up and all of them were medically examined. Thereafter, a compromise was arrived at before the police on 21.12.2005 and she was sent back to matrimonial house but the respondent and other in laws again gave severe beatings to her. She has further deposed that the respondent forced and compelled her to leave the matrimonial house in wearing clothes along with minor children. She has further deposed that all her istridhan articles are in the custody and possession CC No. 49/1/08 PS: Sarai Rohilla Seema Sharma Vs. Krishan Kumar Sharma & Ors. of the respondent and other in laws, who refused to return the same . Therefore, she was compelled to file a complaint before CAW Cell on 31.01.2006. 17. The complainant has not made other respondents a party in the present case, which goes on to suggest that the complainant has made respondent no.2 and 3 a party just to invoke her property rights in the properties belonging to CC No. 49/1/08 PS: Sarai Rohilla Seema Sharma Vs. Krishan Kumar Sharma & Ors. respondent no.2. During cross examination, she has admitted that she had filed a Civil Suit against her in laws to invoke her property rights and said suit has already been dismissed by concerned Ld. Civil Judge. During cross examination, she has further admitted that her elder sister in law was married 10 months before her marriage, which goes on to prove that her sister in law was residing at complainant's matrimonial house for being already married hence, the allegations of the complainant against her are false and incorrect. The complainant has not deposed that her elder sister in law used to reside there only or used to visit her matrimonial house regularly. 19. The complainant has further admitted that a compromise had taken place between her and her husband at PS: Bhajanpura on 21.12.2005, which also goes on to suggest that the grievance of the complainant was mainly against her husband. It be further observed that the respondent no.2 and 3 have been discharged in connected case of FIR No. 220/06, PS: Sarai Rohilla, under section 498 A/406/34 IPC vide order dated 15.12.2009 by Ld. Predecessor and said order was upheld even by the Hon'ble Appellate Court vide its order dated 19.05.2010. In view thereof, the complainant has been unable to prove on record that she had been a victim of domestic violence at the hands of respondent no.2 and 3 and accordingly, they are discharged in the present case. The complainant has prayed for providing reasonable accommodation in any of CC No. 49/1/08 PS: Sarai Rohilla Seema Sharma Vs. Krishan Kumar Sharma & Ors. the two houses owned by the respondents, restraining them to dispossess them from said shared household, alienating or disposing of the shared household or encumbering the same and restraining the respondents from renouncing their rights in the shared household without prior permission. The complainant has not prayed for making provisions for alternative accommodation in her favour.
